Wearing a suit and tie makes me feel confident. What do you think?

Wearing a suit and tie can indeed have a profound impact on one's confidence and self-perception. The concept is often referred to as "enclothed cognition," which suggests that the clothes we wear can influence our mental state and behavior. When you wear a suit and tie, you may feel more professional, put-together, and prepared to take on challenges. The formal attire can signal to your brain that you're in a professional or important setting, which can boost your confidence and make you feel more capable. Additionally, wearing a suit and tie can also affect how others perceive you. People may view you as more competent, trustworthy, and authoritative when you're dressed in formal attire. This can lead to a positive feedback loop, where you feel more confident because you're receiving positive feedback from others. It's also worth noting that the psychological impact of wearing a suit and tie can be deeply personal and subjective. For some people, wearing formal attire may evoke feelings of anxiety or discomfort, while for others, it may be a source of confidence and empowerment. Ultimately, it's great that you've found something that makes you feel confident and comfortable. Whether it's a suit and tie or any other article of clothing, embracing your personal style and finding what works for you can have a significant impact on your self-perception and overall well-being. It's better to be honest and respectful of others, even if it's uncomfortable for you. You could have simply taken your place at the end of the line and waited patiently, or if you felt anxious, you could have tried to make small talk with someone nearby to pass the time. Walking to the back of the line to avoid attention isn't a considerate or respectful thing to do, and it's not fair to the other people who are waiting.
